subject: Orthodox Systems RFP — Load sculpting, variance protocol and measurement plan
messages:
From: Evan Morales <evan.morales@orthodox.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orthodox.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP follow-up: performance measurement details and clarifications

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the materials in the RFP. We had a couple of follow-ups from our infra and procurement teams so we can finalize the benchmarking section: 

1) Can you confirm how Redwood defines the test "request mix"? Specifically, do you simulate multi-turn chat (prefix-heavy) vs stateless single prompt mixes, and can you provide example distributions you recommend?

2) For reported latencies in the RFP (p50/p95/p99), are those measured at the edge (ingress) or at the model-server token emission boundary? Any standardization to compare fairly across vendors is helpful.

3) What typical GPU types and per-GPU QPS numbers do you use for baseline throughput claims? Our ops team needs realistic capacity assumptions (concurrency per GPU at 16k tokens/s, etc.).

4) For load surges: do you run short "spike" tests (30s–2m) vs long soak tests (1–6h)? How do you characterize tail behavior during warm-up?

5) Can Redwood provide a concise test plan we can run in our environment (or a runbook you will run for us)? If you can attach the test harness or traffic profiles that would accelerate our evaluation.

We want to be explicit about measurement windows and acceptance criteria so the procurement team can align on pass/fail for the RFP.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

— Evan Morales
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Orthodox Systems
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Morales <evan.morales@orthodox.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: performance measurement details and clarifications

Evan — great questions. Below is a concise but prescriptive plan we use for RFP benchmarking. I attached the plan, a small runbook tarball, and a set of traffic profiles (see attachments). High level summary first, then details.

High-level approach
- Measurement points: we report latencies at the API ingress (time between request receive and final token emission) and include a secondary breakdown at the model runtime boundary (token emit time plus scheduling overhead). Both are provided so you can compare end-to-end vs model-only.
- Workloads: three canonical mixes — chat-heavy (70% multi-turn with prefix caching simulation), mixed (40% multi-turn / 60% stateless prompts), and stateless (single-shot prompts). Attached sample-traffic-profiles.json.
- Metrics windows: warm-up (10–15m), measurement window (30m for steady-state claims), surge window (3m for short spikes), and soak (4h typical for resilience evidence). We capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, qps, token/s, and system-level signals (GPU utilization, host-side queue depth).
- Burst / spike handling: we run ramp-and-hold spikes (ramp 30s → hold 120s) and stress bursts (5s microbursts) to characterize queueing and prefix-cache miss amplification.

Detailed methodology
1) Traffic composition and priming
   - For multi-turn traffic we create realistic prefix trees from conversation traces; priming runs pre-populate KV cache across replicas to simulate warmed state.
   - We include a category of cold-prefix requests to quantify cold cache tail.
2) Resource baseline and sizing
   - Baseline runs use A100 80GB (logical baseline) and an equivalent Ampere Next variant where available; we also provide quantized 4-bit/8-bit run variants for cost-performance tradeoffs.
   - For each model profile we publish observed steady-state QPS per device and median tokens/s per GPU under our harness.
3) Measurement and signal collection
   - Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured at API edge; model-runtime-latency captured via span instrumentation.
   - Throughput: tokens/s and completed requests/s aggregated in 1s buckets during measurement window.
   - Tail decomposition: we correlate p99 events with queue depth, cache-miss rate, and kernel context-switch events.
4) Acceptance criteria (example)
   - Steady-state: p95 <= 350ms for mixed workload at 80% of published QPS baseline.
   - Surge: system must stay under 1.5x published latency at 80% traffic for the 3m ramp-and-hold test without drop in correctness.
5) Runbook and automation
   - We provide a self-contained harness (dockerized load injector + metrics exporter) and a Redwood-managed option where we run tests in our dedicated lab and share raw traces. See attached runbook tarball (redwood_runbook_templates.tar.gz).

Operational notes
- Canary gating: we recommend a canary run with 10% of target QPS and OOM/failure monitoring before full-scale runs.
- Repeatability: all experiments include seed-controlled synthetic prompts for reproducibility; we provide the seed sets.
- Artifacts: after each trial we deliver raw metrics, aggregated CSVs, flamegraphs for kernel hotspots, and a short executive TL;DR.

Next steps
- If you want Redwood to run the baseline in our lab, we can schedule a 60-minute tech sync and provision the NDAs. If you prefer to run in your environment, the attached harness and profiles should let you reproduce our published numbers.

Attachments:
- orthodox_rfp_perf_plan.pdf (detailed test plan and acceptance criteria)
- redwood_runbook_templates.tar.gz (harness and scripts)
- sample-traffic-profiles.json (traffic mixes we recommend)

Hope this helps — I can join a quick call next week.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Evan Morales <evan.morales@orthodox.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: performance measurement details and clarifications

Stephanie — good write-up. Two quick internal asks before we send the formal reply: 

> From Stephanie: "We provide a self-contained harness (dockerized load injector + metrics exporter) and a Redwood-managed option where we run tests in our dedicated lab and share raw traces."

1) Can you add a short paragraph in the runbook that describes graceful degradation validation? Specifically: simulated node failures (kill/restart), model-fallback switch-over latencies, and queue-shed thresholds. Procurement likes a one-paragraph "failure injection" recipe.
2) Please include an explicit note on KV-cache priming: how many representative prefixes we seed per replica and a suggested priming run duration to achieve steady-state for the p95/p99 claims.
3) Markus — can you confirm the A100 vs Ampere Next delta numbers for the appendix? Evan asked for per-GPU QPS numbers so we should populate the table.

Stephanie — if you can attach an updated small appendix or a 1-page failure-injection snippet to the PDF, I will push this back to Evan and Priya as the formal answer.

Thanks,

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Morales <evan.morales@orthodox.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orthodox.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: performance measurement details and clarifications

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we were after.

Quick replies to the asks: 
- Failure injection paragraph would be useful. Can you include an explicit step that says "simulate one GPU host loss, observe re-routing to warm standby, record switchover latency and p99 delta"? Procurement will gate on a clear switchover objective.
- KV priming guidance: please include a concrete count (e.g., 10k representative prefixes per replica or a priming run of 20 minutes at 0.5x QPS).

Next steps:
1) Stephanie / Ben — can we lock a 60-minute technical sync for Tuesday 2026-12-01 (10am PT)? We want Redwood to run a lab baseline and then provide the artifacts for our procurement evaluation.
2) Priya and I will circulate a template NDA; once in place we can exchange drive access and schedule the lab window.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Evan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Orthodox Systems
